R1.claim: Design A's only remedy for path dependence, `batch_recalibrate`, does not terminate and would not recalibrate anything even if it did. It resets non-anchor ratings and replays the identical log in the identical order, which reproduces the online result bit-for-bit; the joint MLE displayed in the math is never implemented. So the design's '彻底消除漂移' claim has no mechanism behind it.
R1.evidence: design-gemini.md:29-31 says the batch step is meant to '重新拟合一次所有 Checkpoint 的评分 ... 消除路径依赖漂移'; the code at design-gemini.md:41 runs `for p1_name, p2_name, outcome in self.match_history: self.update_match(...)`, while `update_match` ends with `self.match_history.append(...)` — iterating the list it appends to. Repro: `/tmp/a_loop.py` under `timeout 3 /home/amas/.local/src/7g523/.venv/bin/python /tmp/a_loop.py` exits 124 (infinite loop); `/tmp/loop2.py` prints `initial=2 steps=11 len_after=13`, proving appended entries are iterated. Repro on the repo core (500/200 scale): the same 12-game record gives forward {A:480.91, B:513.48, C:502.73} and reversed {A:434.26, B:574.18, C:507.36} (max |Δμ|=60.7), while reset+replay-in-the-same-order returns the forward values exactly (equality True).
R1.fix: Minimal: in the throwaway evaluator, snapshot the log (`for p1,p2,o in tuple(self.match_history)`) and split `_apply_match` (no append) from `update_match` (append), so refit cannot recurse; add a unit test that `batch_recalibrate` terminates and that its output equals the online output (to document that it is a replay). Real fix: either delete the 'eliminates path dependence' claim, or implement an actual batch estimator — maximize Σ log P(outcome | μ) over the full log with anchors hard-pinned, a specified optimizer/tolerance, and the repo's shuffled-log acceptance test (published μ changes <1e-6). The repo's `fit_ratings` is an online replay and provides none of this.
R1.correction: The infinite loop is real: reconstructing Design A's evaluator and running it under `timeout 3` exits 124, because `batch_recalibrate` iterates `self.match_history` while `update_match` appends to it. `batch_recalibrate` is a same-order replay, not the joint MLE shown in §机制三, so it cannot remove path dependence. Caveat the critic omits: the 'bit-for-bit reproduces the online result' sub-claim only holds if every free node was registered at the default prior (25, 8.333); under Design A's own mechanism-2 policy (new checkpoint inherits the incumbent's mu with reset sigma), reset-to-default-mu + replay is NOT the online result (the critic's own /tmp/test_refit_init.py: online new=29.14 vs reset+replay 25.33). Either way the design fails. I could not reproduce the exact 12-game numbers (no generating record was left in /tmp); independent repros on the repo core give max|dmu| ≈ 63 on a 300-game/4-player log and ≈ 63 on a 60-game/3-player log, confirming the order-dependence magnitude (elo.py itself documents order dependence).

Then write the drift taxonomy explicitly with one test each: (i) location/scale (gauge fixed), (ii) order (reversal/permutation), (iii) intransitivity (cross-win cycle), (iv) true population improvement (allowed — measure vs frozen milestones), (v) task/rules change (new scale; bridge via common opponents). R1.claim: Both designs are internally inconsistent about what may move. A freezes anchors but floors legacy σ with σ_min, so legacy μ keeps moving (Δμ ∝ σ²) and nothing becomes a stable coordinate; its mu−3σ gate penalizes exactly the fresh high-σ candidates a gate must test; and σ0=μ0/3 is origin-dependent (can be ≤0). B freezes 'established' μ '永不写' while still letting σ shrink, creating a pseudo-anchor whose claimed confidence rises around a value new data may not correct, and hard-pins 3–5 measured snapshots without ever deriving c_anchor. Note: the hinted 'only-candidate-updates vs zero-sum' is not itself a contradiction — rater outputs are computed before write-back, so discarding the anchor's update does not change the candidate's update; the inflation is the candidate's own Δμ ∝ σ² term.
R1.evidence: design-gemini.md:25-27: 'σ 必须重置为较大的初始 uncertainty（如 σ_0 = \mu_0/3）', '设置 \sigma_{\min}，防止老模型的方差过小而拒绝吸收新对局信息', and the `conservative_rating` docstring '保守等级分，常用于排位与门禁判定 (mu - 3*sigma)'. design-grok.md:72-74: 'established ... 不写 μ ... 只允许 σ 下降' and 'anchor 尺度锚 | 3–5 个冻结快照 | 永不写'; :185 '\mu_{\text{anchor}}=c_{\text{anchor}}\ \text{（钉死）}' with no derivation of c anywhere. Measured Δμ∝σ² on the repo scale: σ=200 vs σ=20 in one 1v1 gives Δμ +81.38 / −0.82 (pool sum ±80.56).
R1.fix: Define one rule per id class, implemented in one place: gauge (definition, σ=0, never updates) / snapshot (converge before publication, then freeze μ and σ together — or keep a separate matchmaking-only uncertainty) / live (never freeze; prior/window). Delete σ_min and mu−3σ gating; gate on deal-clustered expected score. For B, either freeze both μ and σ of established ids or admit μ still moves with damping. Derive c_anchor only from a definition (gauge=0) or carry the anchor's estimation CI as an offset; never pin an unqualified measured value.
R1.correction: Confirmed parts: A does floor legacy sigma via sigma_min (lines 25-27) while still updating legacy mu; the nonzero-sum / Delta-mu ∝ sigma^2 property is real (sigma_new=200 vs sigma_old=20 in one 1v1 gives +81.38/-0.82, pool sum +80.56; sum(dmu)=(sigma_a^2-sigma_b^2)(y-p)/c); A's sigma0=mu0/3 is origin-dependent and would be sigma0=0 on the repo's RandomBot=0 gauge; B freezes established mu while shrinking sigma, and pins c_anchor with no derivation. The clarification that discarding the anchor's update does not change the candidate's update is correct (openskill computes both from pre-game state). Overstated/wrong parts: (a) 'nothing becomes a stable coordinate' is false — A's static engines and milestone anchors are explicitly frozen, non-updating; only free legacy ids move. (b) 'its mu-3sigma gate' conflates the conservative-rating helper with the actual gate, which A specifies as SPRT. (c) B's pseudo-anchor exists in the online layer that B explicitly marks '允许，不对外'; published mu comes from the MLE layer, so the false-confidence harm is largely confined to matching (though §8's tau test does treat online sigma as evidence).

R1.claim: Design A answers an accept/reject gate with its anchor pipeline but cannot answer the repo's leaderboard/ranking question: with RandomBot the single pinned gauge, candidates beat it almost always, so anchor-only games carry near-zero information — ADR-0012 already switched build_ladder's cross default to candidate-vs-candidate for this reason. A has no cross-candidate estimator (the cross-win matrix is only a diagnostic), and its SPRT 'accept ⇒ freeze as dynamic anchor' pins the new checkpoint at the incumbent's inherited μ, contradicting the gate's own +35-Elo evidence; 'dynamic anchor' is itself an oxymoron since an anchor is defined by being frozen.

If an accepted checkpoint is to become a fixed reference, first rate it on its own games — never at the inherited μ — then freeze the measured value with its CI.

A design that freezes a human's μ after N games or hard-pins measured snapshots cannot serve placement, and A's `1500+(mu−25)*400/8.333` / B's `1500+40*(mu−25)` turn repo μ=500 into 24301 / 20500.

R1.claim: Design A's 'whole-history refit' cannot remove path dependence: its reference code (`batch_recalibrate`) resets non-anchors and replays the identical recorded order, which is deterministic and therefore reproduces the exact incremental result; its prose version (anchored PL MLE) is not implemented. Either way it contradicts study.py's frozen-by-default manifest, so its '彻底消除漂移' claim is false.
R1.evidence: design-gemini.md: 'batch_recalibrate ... 重新重置所有非锚点节点的 rating，重新按历史轨迹拟合，消除路径依赖漂移' vs the prose '全局极大似然求解 ... s.t. mu_anchor = C_i'. Repro (repo scale 500/200): 8-game fit on the same order is bit-identical on reset+replay ('replay-identical: True'), while reversing the same games moves x by dmu=-36.87 and y by +29.96 (placement stop_ci=50). src/seven523/elo.py:218 'The update is order-dependent'; src/seven523/study.py:8-11 'freezes ratings by default ... explicit refit=True decision'.
R1.fix: Delete batch_recalibrate entirely. For 'did it improve', use the order-free deal-clustered `duel.paired_duel_stats` / `combine_duel_seeds` (tools/head_to_head.py). Only if a global order-free table is genuinely required, add a pure offline anchored-MLE module/tool (no torch/numpy/IO) and amend ADR-0011 explicitly; never auto-rewrite frozen manifest levels.
R1.correction: Core claim verified: reset+replay of the identical recorded order is deterministic and leaves ratings bit-identical to the incremental run, so 'whole-history refit' removes no path dependence and the 彻底消除漂移 promise is false. I reproduced replay-identical=True and the order sensitivity (my seed: x moved -47.8 / y +47.8, critic's -36.9/+30.0; signs and mechanism match, exact figures depend on the unreproduced game sequence). Two critical missing caveats: (1) the literal batch_recalibrate in design-gemini.md is actually BUGGY, not replay-identical: it iterates `for ... in self.match_history` while update_match appends to that same list, so the list grows every iteration and the loop never terminates (I demonstrated 12 capped iterations grew history 3->15; unbounded it hangs). The critic's 'replay-identical: True' comes from a silently corrected implementation, not the design's code. (2) The study.py contradiction is indirect: Design A never touches traces/study (it refits in-memory EvaluatorNode ratings), and merge_manifest's freeze rule is a project principle, not a call that batch_recalibrate makes. The claim that batch_recalibrate 'reproduces the exact incremental result' also holds only when non-anchor nodes start at default_mu/default_sigma; register_node permits custom mu/sigma, which reset discards, so in that case batch differs from incremental (still deterministically order-dependent). The recommended fix (delete it; use duel.paired_duel_stats/combine_duel_seeds) is sound.

R1.claim: Grok's central constant `tau=0` cannot be adopted by this repo: FitConfig rejects tau<=0, and combining tau=0 with the repo's documented anchor representation (pinned mu, sigma=0, ADR-0011) makes openskill 6.2.0's rate() raise ZeroDivisionError. Grok only avoids this by giving anchors sigma>0, i.e. by not using the repo's pinned anchors.
R1.evidence: design-grok.md:82 'tau = 0 # 关键：关掉动态因子', :110 'tau=0.0'. Repro 1: `FitConfig(tau=0.0)` -> ValueError: 'tau must be positive and finite, got 0.0' (src/seven523/elo.py:143-146, docstring:133 'A positive tau is required'). Repro 2: `PlackettLuce(mu=500,sigma=200,beta=100,tau=0).rate([[x],[anchor(sigma=0)]])` -> ZeroDivisionError at openskill/models/weng_lin/plackett_luce.py:879 (division by `team_i.sigma_squared`, which is 0 for a sigma=0 team with tau=0). ADR-0011:16 keeps tau as the dynamic term replacing the retired window.
R1.fix: Keep FitConfig tau>0 (default sigma/100=2.0) and keep anchors at sigma=0; anchor updates are already discarded in fit_ratings (elo.py:259), so no write policy is needed. If a frozen-snapshot mode is desired, add it at the orchestration layer (Prior/anchors), never as tau=0 inside the core.
R1.correction: Both repros verified independently: FitConfig(tau=0.0) raises ValueError 'tau must be positive and finite, got 0.0' (src/seven523/elo.py:144-146), and PlackettLuce(mu=500,sigma=200,beta=100,tau=0).rate([[x],[anchor sigma=0]]) raises ZeroDivisionError at openskill/models/weng_lin/plackett_luce.py:879 (`sigma**2 / team_i.sigma_squared`). tau=0 is central to Design B (design-grok.md:82,110,233), so it cannot be adopted inside this repo's core. R1.claim: There is no statistical accept gate: the only existing stop/accept logic is bootstrap's fixed progress_margin on an order-dependent fit delta (`productive` + `patience`), while the deal-clustered CI machinery in duel/combine_duel_seeds is not wired to any gate. On repo scale beta=100, p=0.55 corresponds to delta-mu = sqrt(2)*100*Phi^-1(0.55) ~= 17.8 rating points, not 35 (35 is 400*log10(.55/.45)). duel.py already produces per-deal clustered winrate plus an exact sign p-value.

R1.claim: Both designs define "no drift" as "anchor mu never changes" and implement it by skipping anchor writeback, so the acceptance test passes because of the if-statement, not because the ruler is stable. Hard-pinned anchors (sigma=0) freeze their own measurement/selection error into the scale, and an anchor whose true strength moves (silent backend update, mis-freeze) is undetectable by construction.
R1.evidence: Grok design-grok.md §8 test table: "锚点不动 | 插入一个比锚点强 1.5β 的新模型，打 200 场 | 锚点 μ 变化 = 0（在线层写回）"; §9.2 "锚点必须是冻结权重/冻结 API 版本". Add a pre-registered "ruler audit" to every publication: anchor-vs-anchor and anchor-vs-RandomBot games on a disjoint deal set; fail publication if anchor residuals move outside a declared CI; publish anchor residual drift as a first-class metric.
R1.correction: Core holds but two attributions are wrong. (1) Neither design hard-pins sigma=0: Gemini's EvaluatorNode freezes an anchor at its registration (mu, _anchor_sigma) and discards the update, and Grok freezes the snapshot's (mu, sigma); sigma=0 is the repo's elo.py convention (elo.py:14, fit_ratings initial()). Also, with the repo's tau>0, openskill's rate() injects tau into every participant (plackett_luce.py:586-593), so a sigma=0 anchor is internally sigma=tau during the update and only re-reported as 0 by elo.py. (2) 'Both designs define no drift as anchor mu never changes' is an overstatement: Grok explicitly makes an order-independent anchored PL-MLE the published layer and lists six acceptance tests; only the '锚点不动' test is tautological. The valid, important part: that test is satisfied by the if-statement, not by ruler stability; a measured checkpoint anchor freezes its own selection/measurement error and cannot detect its own strength drift; ADR-0012 already retired greedy=1315 for exactly this 'stale preset coordinate' failure. Relevance: high, but the repo currently pins only the exogenous RandomBot (ANCHOR_ID/ANCHOR_RATING in arena.py; DEFAULT_ANCHOR_RATING in ladder.py), so this only bites if the designs' measured checkpoint anchors are adopted. RUNG_PRIOR_SD=30 in placement/estimator.py confirmed.

R1.claim: batch_recalibrate is not the claimed whole-history MLE: it resets free nodes to the default prior and replays the same order-dependent online update, so path dependence is untouched and register-time priors are silently discarded. Worse, update_match appends to match_history while batch_recalibrate iterates that same list, so the refit never terminates and memory grows without bound.

Repro (/tmp, timeout 5): `python - <<loop pattern>>` -> "processed 1e6 iterations, len(history) = 1000001" (never exits). Repo elo.py:218 "The update is order-dependent: games is the history, and later 牌局 carry more weight through the dynamics term." Probe /tmp/probe_drift.py: forward vs reversed history gives a=458.1 vs 521.0 (order matters); reset+replay over the same history is byte-identical to a fresh single pass (so the reset adds nothing); with Prior(mu=520) the online value is 631.7 but reset+replay gives 617.9 (the prior is gone).

If the online replay is kept, iterate a snapshot (`for rec in tuple(self.match_history)`), never append during refit, and delete the path-independence claim. Persist (seed, seats, scores, rules_version) and each id's initial prior to disk so refits are reproducible, and bound cost with per-outcome-pattern sufficient statistics instead of an unbounded in-RAM pair list.
R1.correction: Mechanism confirmed; only the illustrative numbers did not reproduce. batch_recalibrate does reset every non-anchor to self.default_mu/default_sigma (discarding register-time priors), then replays the same update_match in the same order, so path dependence is untouched; the design prose claims an MLE it does not implement. The for-loop over self.match_history while update_match appends to it genuinely never terminates and grows without bound: bounded repro reached 200,000 iterations with len(history)=200,030. My probe with Prior(mu=520) vs a distant anchor did not give 631.7/617.9: with all-wins the Plackett-Luce update saturates, so online mu stayed 520.0 while reset+replay from the default prior gave 35.46; the prior-discard and 'reset+replay == fresh default-prior pass' (35.462229155765144 both) are confirmed. Because the loop never returns, the method has no final state at all, so the whole 'batch refit' is dead code plus unbounded memory, not merely a weak refit. Fatal for the design as written.

R1.claim: Grok's sigma<2.5 certification is unreachable in the regime it exists for. Against a distant pinned anchor p->1, the Weng-Lin update term is proportional to p(1-p)->0, so sigma stalls (and with tau>0 can rise); a frontier model stays in probation with an inflated, prior/n-driven mu, or is certified on games that carried almost no information. Freezing established mu while sigma keeps shrinking makes a stale location look steadily more certain, and Grok's tau=0 is rejected by this repo's seam.
R1.evidence: design-grok.md: "σ* = 2.5" and lifecycle table "established ... 不写 μ（或只写 5–10% 阻尼）| 只允许 σ 下降"; §5 code freezes established mu. openskill .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/openskill/models/weng_lin/plackett_luce.py:836 `delta += i_mu_over_ce_over_sum_q * (1 - i_mu_over_ce_over_sum_q) / a[q]`; :880/:888 `sigma *= math.sqrt(max(1 - (sigma**2/team_i.sigma_squared)*delta*weight, self.kappa))`, i.e. information vanishes as p->1. Probe /tmp/probe_saturation.py (repo scale sigma0=200, beta=100, tau=2), all-wins vs pinned mu=0 anchor: n=40 mu=733.5 sigma=136.6; n=200 881.1/108.4; n=1000 1046.9/96.9; n=5000 1339.5/119.1 - sigma never approaches the sigma*/sigma0-ratio equivalent (~60). Bernoulli true p=0.90: mean fitted mu 349.8 at n=200 vs 322.4 at n=800 (same model, different n). Repo docs/experiments/human-elo-10-games-research.md:301 "超过 ~1600 后信息量随饱和塌缩"; elo.py:145 rejects `tau <= 0.0` ("tau must be positive and finite"), so Grok's "tau=0" cannot be expressed through the existing FitConfig seam.

Gate on held-out calibration (log-loss/Brier against anchors), not sigma. Report frontier comparisons via same-deal head-to-head (duel.py) with deal-clustered CIs. If tau=0 is wanted, add an explicit static-snapshot flag to FitConfig rather than weakening the invariant, and re-sync established mu from the MLE layer at each publication.
R1.correction: The saturation mechanism and the source citations are exact (plackett_luce.py:836 delta term proportional to p(1-p); :880/:888 sigma shrink), and I reproduced the critic's repo-scale tau=2 numbers bit-for-bit: n=40 733.5/136.6, n=200 881.1/108.4, n=1000 1046.9/96.9, n=5000 1339.5/119.1, sigma then rising (175 at n=20000), never near the 60-equivalent threshold. The Bernoulli n-dependence reproduced too (mean fitted mu 355.4 at n=200 vs 327.4 at n=800 for true p=0.90, ~28-point gap). Correction: 'unreachable' is too strong. Grok's tau=0 makes sigma monotone non-increasing, and it does cross sigma*=2.5, but only after ~128,000 all-win games against a distant anchor (I measured first crossing at n=128,230, vs the design's N*=40) -- i.e. unreachable on any practical horizon, not in the limit. More importantly, the design also plays 40% near-mu peers, whose near-50/50 games are informative and would shrink sigma, so sigma<2.5 is not universally unreachable; the robust claim is that sigma-certification is not a scale-identifiability guarantee and that freezing established mu while sigma keeps shrinking (Grok §5: mu frozen, sigma=min) overstates confidence in a stale location. Additional critical caveat the critic only half-states: tau=0 combined with the repo's sigma=0 anchors raises ZeroDivisionError in openskill (0/0 team variance), so Grok's tau=0 cannot even run against the repo's anchor convention, not merely be expressed through FitConfig; FitConfig rejects tau<=0 (elo.py:145) confirmed.

R1.claim: The SPRT gate has no stated alpha/beta, no one-shot or pre-registration rule, and no log of rejected candidates. R1.claim: Anchoring fixes only the additive location gauge; it does not identify the scale. But the application to Grok is overstated: Grok fixes beta=25/6 in his constants and his batch objective maximises only over mu, so one pinned anchor pins the location gauge AND fixed beta pins the scale - his 'one degree of freedom, one anchor=25' is correct as stated. The genuine defects are Grok's table claim that pinning anchors gives 'Σμ 有约束' (false: a single anchor constrains only location), and the operational requirement that beta/sigma conventions be held fixed across fits. R1.claim: For 2-player Weng-Lin, sum of delta-mu = (sigma_a^2 - sigma_b^2)(y - p)/c exactly. It is zero whenever the two sigmas are equal, and its conditional expectation is zero whenever the model's p equals the true win probability; so 'delta-mu is nonzero-sum, therefore the pool inflates' is a non sequitur. It is a mean-zero redistribution/random walk whose sign follows the outcome. tau is added symmetrically to both sides and cannot create this asymmetry. The proposed rule 'subtract the game's mean delta-mu for all-probation games' is an arbitrary gauge projection that biases updates.
R1.evidence: design-grok.md line 37: 'delta-mu proportional to sigma^2, not zero-sum ... pool total mu rises ... this is the main cause of rating inflation/deflation'; line 142 recommends 'subtract this game's mean delta-mu'. /tmp/test_sum_dmu.py verifies the closed form to ~1e-15: sigmas (1,3), y=1 gives sum=-0.598134=(1^2-3^2)(1-0.5)/c; sigmas (2,2) gives sum=0.000000 for both outcomes; (0.5,4), y=1 gives -1.103021. The expected drift E[sum]=(sigma_a^2-sigma_b^2)(p_true-p_hat)/c vanishes at calibration; systematic scale movement comes from the unpinned gauge, entry priors, or misspecification, not from the instantaneous sum.
R1.fix: Remove the mean-subtraction rule and the inflation diagnosis. Keep the pinned anchor as the location gauge, and validate the online layer with a reliability/calibration check (predicted p vs realized win rate) instead of pool sums. If an all-free pool mean must be fixed, do it once as an explicit gauge convention, not per game.
R1.correction: Core claim verified exactly. For 2P Weng-Lin, sum(Δμ) = (σ_a²-σ_b²)(y-p)/c to ~1e-15 (sigmas (1,3), y=1 -> -0.598134; (2,2) -> 0; (0.5,4), y=1 -> -1.103021), and E[sum]=(σ_a²-σ_b²)(q-p)/c vanishes iff the model is calibrated. tau adds τ² to both variances and leaves σ_a²-σ_b² unchanged, so it cannot create the asymmetry. Therefore Grok's 'Δμ is nonzero-sum, therefore the pool inflates' is a non sequitur: the instantaneous sum is a mean-zero redistribution whose sign follows the outcome; only miscalibration, entry priors, selection, or an unpinned gauge move the scale. Caveat on the fix wording: subtracting the per-game mean is a gauge choice, not strictly a statistical 'bias'; but in Grok's anchored system it does fight the anchor gauge, so using the pinned anchor plus a reliability/calibration check is the right replacement. This is Design B's reasoning; the repo's own online layer has the same property and does not claim otherwise.

R1.claim: tau is an explicit forgetting/window parameter, not a drift source, and tau=0 does not make replay order-free. With tau=0 sigma collapses by a slow power law (self-freezing ratings); with tau>0 it reaches a steady-state sigma. Order sensitivity is essentially identical for the two. The repo's FitConfig docstring is only asymptotically true, far beyond its ladder lengths. Grok's acceptance test 'tau off: sigma does not rise' is vacuous given his own min(sig0,new_sig) write-back.
R1.evidence: src/seven523/elo.py:130-135: 'A positive tau is required: a zero dynamics term makes the standard update degenerate after enough games.' /tmp/test_tau_order.py (sigma0=200, beta=100, equal opponents): tau=0 sigma = 193.6 (1 game), 149.96 (10), 56.62 (100), 20.89 (1000), 7.286 (20000), late |delta-mu|=0.183; tau=2 sigma plateaus at 35.24 with |delta-mu|=3.87. Order sensitivity across 20 permutations: 112.2 (tau=0) vs 114.8 (tau=2); forward-vs-reversed: 37.24 vs 37.74. Repo default games_per_anchor=100 (ladder.py:118), where tau=0 still leaves sigma=56.16 (200 games: 40.26), so 'degenerate' is not reached in practice. Grok line 224 test pairs with line 41's `m.sigma = min(sig0, new_sig)`. Also openskill 6.2.0 plackett_luce.py:587 `tau = tau if tau else self.tau`: a model built with tau=2 gives identical sigma with and without an explicit rate(..., tau=0.0) (verified).
R1.fix: Declare tau as the intended window: use tau=0 (plus freezing, or an MLE layer that has no tau) for the static published scale, and keep the repo's tau>0 online ladder as a deliberate recency window (its test_recent_games_dominate_old_form relies on that). Never sell tau as an order-independence fix; if a per-call tau=0 is ever needed, build a tau=0 model because of openskill's `if tau` fallback.
R1.correction: All numbers reproduced. tau=0 sigma trajectory (equal opponents): 193.57 (1), 149.96 (10), 56.62 (100), 20.89 (1000), 7.29 (20000), with late |Δμ| falling below 0.2; tau=2 plateaus at ~35.24 with stable |Δμ|~3.9. 20-permutation order spread 112.2 (tau=0) vs 114.8 (tau=2); forward-vs-reversed 37.24 vs 37.74, so tau does not buy order-independence. open skill 6.2.0 line 587 `tau = tau if tau else self.tau` confirmed: a tau=2 model gives identical sigma when rate(..., tau=0.0) is passed (193.581634 both). Grok's acceptance row 'tau off: sigma does not rise' is indeed unfalsifiable given the established write-back `m.sigma = min(sig0, new_sig)`. Critical missing caveats: (a) the repo cannot express tau=0 at all - FitConfig raises for tau<=0 (elo.py:144-146); (b) with the repo's sigma=0 anchors, openskill raises ZeroDivisionError when tau=0 (inside `rate`, sigma is lifted to sqrt(0+tau^2)=tau, so tau=0 leaves sigma_squared=0 and `sigma**2/team_i.sigma_squared` is 0/0) - verified. So the critic's 'use tau=0' recommendation is not a drop-in constant change. The FitConfig docstring is asymptotically true, not reached at the repo's ladder lengths.

R1.claim: Tie handling is incomplete for this repo, whose card games tie often. openskill's tied-rank mu-averaging branch is dead code because it compares already-mutated objects, so tie updates are nonzero-sum whenever sigmas differ. Gemini's (p1,p2,outcome) history cannot represent the repo's N-seat score games at all, and Grok's 'PL/BT MLE over ranks' has no specified tie likelihood (plain ranked BT/PL treats ties as strict orderings unless the likelihood is tie-aware).
R1.evidence: openskill plackett_luce.py:895-908: `modified_player = original_teams[i][j]; modified_player.mu = mu; ... avg_mu_change = sum(result[i][0].mu - original_teams[i][0].mu ...)`; /tmp/test_tie_deadcode.py loads the shipped .py and prints 'result objects are the same objects as the (deep-copied) input: True', so the difference is identically zero. Draw with (mu,sigma)=(27,1) vs (23,3), ranks=[0,0]: delta_a=-0.021717, delta_b=+0.195450 (the intended average branch would assign both +0.086866). Repo handles ties/scores at elo.py:256 `model.rate(teams, scores=[float(score) ...])`, with tests/test_elo.py::test_draws_leave_equal_ratings_unchanged and ::test_multiplayer_games_rank_by_score_and_handle_ties. design-gemini.md line 41: `match_history: List[Tuple[str,str,int]] # (p1,p2,outcome...)` and `ranks=[0,1]/[1,0]/[0,0]`; design-grok.md section 7 objective `max_mu sum log P(ranks | mu)`.
R1.fix: Keep the repo's record shape (seed, seats, scores) and score-derived ranks. For a published batch fit, use a tie-aware likelihood (Weng-Lin's rank-tie update or Davidson/BT-with-draws) and add tie tests; do not build a 2-seat-only rating path, and state explicitly how ties enter Grok's MLE.
R1.correction: Two of the three sub-claims are solid. (1) The tie-averaging branch is dead: in `_compute`, `original_teams = teams` is only an alias, `modified_player = original_teams[i][j]` is mutated in the update loop, `result[i][j]` is that same object, so `avg_mu_change = result[i][0].mu - original_teams[i][0].mu == 0` (instrumented subclass confirms result objects `is` the deep-copied input). A draw with (mu,sigma)=(27,1) vs (23,3), ranks [0,0] gives Δ=(-0.021717,+0.195450), whereas the intended average would be +0.086866 for both. (2) Gemini's `(p1,p2,outcome)` history cannot represent the repo's N-seat score games at all. Refuted part: the 'so tie updates are nonzero-sum' causal link is wrong - assigning both tied teams (da+db)/2 preserves the total (2*(da+db)/2 = da+db), so the dead branch affects per-player symmetry, not the sum; ties are nonzero-sum whenever sigmas differ regardless of the branch. Also, 'plain ranked BT/PL treats ties as strict orderings' is imprecise: openskill's PL accepts tied ranks (that is the branch in question); what is genuinely missing is a specified tie likelihood in Grok's MLE. The repo does exercise ties via scores (elo.py:256; tests/test_elo.py::test_draws_leave_equal_ratings_unchanged and ::test_multiplayer_games_rank_by_score_and_handle_ties), and those tests only cover equal-mu/equal-prior ties, so the asymmetric-sigma tie case is untested.

R1.claim: openskill's WL update uses the logistic Plackett-Luce probability, but predict_win (used by the repo's expected_score/duel and by Grok's calibration acceptance tests and progress reporting) uses a probit. The two differ by about 4.6 percentage points at a 100-mu gap on the repo scale, so a probability calibrated against one is mis-calibrated against the other.
R1.evidence: openskill plackett_luce.py: `_sum_q` uses math.exp(mu/c) (logistic), `predict_win` uses phi_major (probit). For A=(mu=600,sigma=200), B=(mu=500,sigma=200), beta=100: c=316.227766; rate's implied p back-computed from delta-mu=53.328062 is 1 - 53.328062*316.227766/200^2 = 0.578405, while predict_win returns 0.624085. ADR-0011 decision 2 claims expected_score '就是 PL 的 predict_win' and the alternatives bullet sells that as '保证单一真相'. design-grok.md lines 201-206 uses predict_win for progress and calibration.
R1.fix: Pick one link and say so. For WL updates, calibrate/report the logistic probability implied by rate (or explicitly document predict_win's probit as an approximation and calibrate it too); do not use predict_win as the target when checking that a WL fit is calibrated.
R1.correction: Reproduced exactly. For A=(600,200), B=(500,200), beta=100: c=sqrt(200^2+100^2+200^2+100^2)=316.227766, rate's Δμ_a=53.328062, back-implied p=1-53.328062*316.227766/200^2=0.578405, which equals logistic(100/c); predict_win returns Phi(100/c)=0.624085, a 4.568 pp gap. rate() uses the exponential/softmax (logistic) link in `_sum_q`/`_compute`; predict_win uses `phi_major` (probit). The repo's `expected_score` wraps predict_win (ADR-0011 decision 2; tests/test_elo.py::test_expected_score_matches_the_plackett_luce_gaussian explicitly asserts the Gaussian CDF), and Grok uses predict_win for progress/calibration. So a fit calibrated on the logistic update can be mis-calibrated under the reported probit. Severity minor is fair, but it is real and directly affects Grok's calibration acceptance rows and the repo's D3 pairing/reporting.

R1.claim: Design A's anchors do not implement its own hard-anchor spec: the prose requires anchors with sigma0=0, but register_node defaults anchor sigma to default_sigma=8.333 unless the caller passes 0, restore_anchor is never called, and to_elo_scale ignores its scale parameter and hardcodes 400/8.333.
R1.evidence: design-gemini.md line 19: anchors are '硬性固定的评分 (mu0, sigma0=0)'; line 41 register_node: `init_sigma = sigma if sigma is not None else self.default_sigma`; to_elo_scale signature takes `scale: float = 400/math.log(10)` but returns `(node.mu - self.default_mu) * (400.0/8.333)`. Running the design's class: `ev.register_node('stockfish', mu=25.0, is_anchor=True)` prints 'anchor stored sigma: 8.333'. `grep -c restore_anchor critique/design-gemini.md` = 1 (definition only, no call site).
R1.fix: Default anchors to sigma=0 (or make sigma required for anchors), actually use or delete restore_anchor, and either honor the scale argument or remove it. A sigma>0 'hard' anchor is a soft reference and changes the update geometry.
R1.correction: Confirmed. `register_node('stockfish', mu=25.0, is_anchor=True)` stores sigma=default_sigma=8.333, not 0 (verified); `grep -c restore_anchor` = 1, its definition only, no call site; `to_elo_scale(name, scale=...)` ignores `scale` and returns `target_base + (node.mu-default_mu)*(400.0/8.333)` (to_elo_scale(25, scale=1)=1500.0; (26, scale=999)=1548.0019). Caveats: the anchor's mu is still effectively hard because `update_match` discards anchor updates and `EvaluatorNode.mu` returns the stored `_anchor_mu`; and openskill's `rate()` already deep-copies and returns new objects without mutating inputs (verified), so `restore_anchor` is redundant rather than load-bearing. The real defect is that an anchor with sigma>0 is a soft reference (it changes c and the opponent's update geometry). This is a Design A (chess/AlphaZero) issue; the repo instead pins anchors via fit_ratings with sigma returned as exactly 0.

R1.claim: Design A's 'Batch Whole-History Refit' neither removes path dependence nor even terminates as written. `batch_recalibrate()` iterates `self.match_history` while `update_match()` appends to that same list (unbounded loop); with the iteration fixed to a snapshot, reset-and-replay of the identical chronological log reproduces the incremental ratings bit-for-bit, so no global fit has occurred and the estimator is still order-dependent. It also silently discards every node's custom prior (resets to default_mu/default_sigma).
R1.evidence: Design text: '使用全历史博弈日志（Full Match History Log）重新拟合一次所有 Checkpoint 的评分 ... 消除路径依赖漂移', with code 'for p1_name, p2_name, outcome in self.match_history: self.update_match(...)' and update_match ends 'self.match_history.append((p1_name, p2_name, outcome))'. Repro /tmp/a_batch_refit.py (openskill 6.2.0) observed: '(a) as-written loop: history grew 200 -> 20201 rows after 20001 iterations; loop is unbounded (aborted)'; '(b) snapshot-replay ratings identical to incremental: True'; 'max |mu_fwd - mu_rev|: 1.4569' on A's 25-point scale; 'custom-prior E: incremental mu=40.0000 -> after refit mu=25.0000'. The repo's own core agrees replay is path-dependent: elo.py docstring 'The update is order-dependent: games is the history, and later 牌局 carry more weight through the dynamics term.'
R1.fix: Use a real order-invariant batch fit — Plackett–Luce/BT MLE over the full log solved to convergence with anchor constraints/priors (Design B's §7 shape, or Coulom WHR) — as the public scale, and keep the online replay only for matchmaking, labelled as such. If a sequential replay is kept, snapshot the history before iterating and stop calling it a refit; also never reset nodes to defaults (preserve each node's prior or pass it explicitly).
R1.correction: Confirmed by reproduction. batch_recalibrate() does `for ... in self.match_history: self.update_match(...)` while update_match ends with self.match_history.append(...); Python's list iterator advances by index over the growing list, so the loop is unbounded. My repro: history 5 -> 200,005 rows after 200,001 guarded iterations, never terminates. A snapshot-replay of the identical log from the same default priors reproduces the incremental ratings bit-for-bit (verified True), so it is not a global fit and remains order-dependent: replaying my 200-game log reversed changed mu by up to 1.85 on the 25-scale (the critic's 1.46 is just a different random log). It also resets every non-anchor to default_mu/default_sigma, silently discarding custom priors (my node E registered at mu=40.0 with no games came back at 25.0), and update_match even re-appends history during the replay. Fix is correct. Caveat for the project: the repo's fit_ratings is *documented* as an order-dependent chronological replay (elo.py:186-190), so this pseudo-code is a strictly worse re-implementation of an existing deliberate design, and the repo's only batch/global estimator was the retired BT-MAP (ADR-0006); a real PL/BT MLE (or Coulom WHR) as a separate public-scale layer is the right missing piece.

R1.claim: The SPRT gate is under-specified and mis-tuned: H1 is p>=0.55 (≈+35 Elo), and no alpha, beta, LLR bounds or max-games are given. Under the conventional alpha=beta=0.05 reading, a genuinely improving +10 Elo net is accepted only 22% of the time, +15 Elo 40%, +20 Elo 61%; only >=+35 Elo reaches ~95%. That is a +35-Elo filter, not a pass/fail regression gate, and the per-test false-accept rate is not budgeted across many candidate nets.
R1.evidence: Design §3: 'H_0: 胜率 p \le 0.50（ Elo 增量 \le 0）' / 'H_1: 胜率 p \ge 0.55（ Elo 增量 \ge 35）' and '当 SPRT 判定接受（Accept）时，说明新模型实力显著超越上代'. No error rates or bounds appear anywhere in §3. Repro /tmp/a_sprt.py (20k trials, alpha=beta=0.05, upper bound log(19), lower log(1/19)) observed: 0 Elo -> P(accept H1)=0.048; 10 Elo -> 0.220; 15 -> 0.398; 20 -> 0.608; 35 -> 0.954 (H1 boundary maps to 34.9 Elo).
R1.fix: Pre-register the test: alpha=beta=0.05 (or 0.01 for auto-promotion), explicit LLR bounds log((1-beta)/alpha), a max-game cap, and H1 set to the smallest effect worth acting on. For this repo pick H1 from its own power table (evaluation-protocol-validation.md §5: 20 Elo requires ~807 paired deals for 80% power, 10 Elo ~3226) and run the test on deal twins (pentanomial/per-deal scores) rather than iid games. Log LLR, games and realized error over the run; if many nets are gated, use alpha-spending or an always-valid sequential test.

R1.claim: The gate decides pool membership and, on pass, the new best/anchor candidate, so all measured ratings are computed on a winner-selected population: the accepted net's measured gain is upward-biased by selection (winner's curse), then reused as the next baseline and possibly frozen as an anchor; rejected checkpoints are discarded and never rated. With hundreds of gates at the conventional 5% per-test error the run has essentially no family-wise false-accept bound, so the 'progress curve' of accepted bests is monotone-by-construction evidence.
R1.evidence: Design flow: 'SPRT 测试 (vs 当前 Best 模型) ... (Fail / Reject) 丢弃该 Checkpoint ... 1. 替换为当前 Best 模型 2. 注册进 Openskill 评估池' and line 57 '并冻结其作为新的动态锚点候选'; no per-run error budget is stated. /tmp/a_sprt.py shows the per-test false accept is 0.048 at 0 Elo under alpha=0.05, i.e. ~1-in-20 gates if the null holds.
R1.fix: Separate promotion from rating: rate every checkpoint, including rejected ones, on a common fixed schedule (gauge + frozen opponent panel) before/independently of the gate. After a gate pass, require an independent confirmatory fixed-sample comparison with a fresh seed/deal set against a fixed reference before promoting or freezing anything; report the gate's realized false-accept rate and the shrinkage between gate-sample and confirm-sample Elo. Budget family-wise error across a training run (lower alpha for auto-promotion, alpha-spending/always-valid tests) and keep rejected nets as pool opponents for diversity (the repo already has PfspController for this).
R1.correction: Confirmed. The design flow literally says SPRT pass -> '替换为当前 Best 模型', '注册进 Openskill 评估池', '与锚点池对弈', and line 57 '并冻结其作为新的动态锚点候选'; failures are '丢弃该 Checkpoint'. Thus only winners enter the rated pool, the gate gain is conditioned on passing (winner's curse), that inflated value becomes the next baseline/anchor, rejected checkpoints are never rated, and at 5% per test hundreds of gates give essentially no family-wise bound (1-0.95^n). The fix (rate every checkpoint on a fixed common schedule, confirm promotion on a fresh fixed sample, keep rejected nets as PFSP opponents, budget family-wise error) is correct and repo-aligned. Caveat: the selection effect mainly makes the *baseline* harder to beat (conservative for future promotions) while inflating reported progress; 'the progress curve is monotone-by-construction' is loose, since each new best is only compared to the then-current best, though the evidence-selection point stands.

R1.claim: Design A uses one adaptive loop for both selection and measurement: opponents are chosen by -|mu_cand - mu_opp| + 5 (anchor bonus), 5 games per call, and those outcomes immediately update the published ratings. Fixed-opponent measurement is the standard reason fishtest pairs every test against the same master and Lc0 runs gauntlets.

R1.claim: Design A correctly identifies intransitivity as the 1-D failure mode, but 'measure matrix asymmetry and loops' with no null model is not a detector: under adaptive nearest-mu pairing the weak-vs-weak pairs where cycles live are rarely or never played, and apparent cycles arise from sampling noise in transitive populations. 'Train exploiter models' is a training intervention, not an evaluation fix; the repo's own answer is seat-paired head-to-head with deal clustering, optionally with a population-average model.

Repo duel.py:8 'cluster the statistics by 牌 (the twin pair)'; elo-reliability-audit.md §6.5: '候选比较优先 head-to-head + 同牌 CRN ... 方差远小于各自对锚点的绝对分'. The §4 'Cross-Win Matrix' has no test statistic, CI or multiplicity control.
R1.fix: Report a full pairwise matchup matrix with deal-clustered CIs (sign test or cluster bootstrap) from a schedule that guarantees pair coverage (the repo's cross games do this); declare a cycle only when the margin is significant after multiplicity control, and add a population/Nash-average (e.g. Balduzzi-style) or 2-D rating as the diagnostic when cycles are real. Keep exploiters as a training response only.

Overstated/wrong: the specific assertion that 'the weak-vs-weak pairs where cycles live are rarely or never played' is unsupported — nearest-μ pairing schedules weak-vs-weak games *more* often, and intransitive cycles are not a weak-vs-weak phenomenon; the genuine gap is sparse coverage of the full pairwise matrix. R1.claim: The lifecycle rule 'established mu 不写 / anchor-frozen 永不写' is incompatible with how this repo consumes ratings. The arena re-rates the whole pool every round and trims on those fresh ratings, placement re-fits the human every session, matchmaking reads the posterior, and the human plan explicitly leaves human non-stationarity open. Freezing established mu makes eviction, parent choice, opponent selection and human placement run on stale numbers; the repo's one experiment that tested fixed published values found them wrong (lvl4 off by -59.7) and only an explicit --refit fixed them.

Keep the online/pool rating updating with the repo's tau>0 and keep human placement using window/forgetting semantics; only a published, estimator-versioned board may be frozen (what study.merge_manifest(refit=False) already does). Record freeze provenance so a later re-measure can supersede it, and never feed frozen numbers into trim/matchmaking.
R1.correction: Core is right: the repo's online layer is the live rating. bootstrap._mass_rate/rate_pool re-fit the whole pool with tau>0 and immediately Pool.apply_fit (pool.py:340) and Pool.trim (pool.py:319) off those fresh numbers; bootstrap forks members strongest-first by mu (bootstrap.py:5-11) and arena/qualify schedules are built per fresh round; placement's select_opponent is Fisher/Thompson on mu/sigma and fit_session re-fits every session; human-elo-plan.md:83 leaves non-stationarity open. Design B is also internally inconsistent: §3 (line 20-21) says the online layer 'allows drift', then §4/§5 (72-74, 130, 245) freeze established mu. Freezing it does corrupt trim/fork/placement. Two caveats the critic overstates: (1) 'anchor-frozen never writes' already matches the repo — fit_ratings pins anchors at sigma=0 and skips them (elo.py:244, 275); the conflict is specifically the freeze of non-anchor 'established' ids. (2) The lvl4 1489.4->1429.7, -59.7 case was the old plan_games seat-phase bug (audit §5.4, ladder-rerating-paired.md §2.3), not rating drift, and it was fixed by exactly the published-ledger refit path (study.merge_manifest refit=True) the critic says is fine — so it supports the critic's own proposed fix rather than proving freezing per se is wrong.

R1.claim: Design B's central justification is factually wrong, and the invariant it claims to import is unattainable. Chatbot Arena does not pin 3-5 anchors with frozen mu, does not keep old models' published values fixed, and did not switch to BT 'because online Elo drifts': its BT model fixes one gauge (xi_1=0), re-fits every model from the full battle log, and its deployed intervals are sandwich robust SEs, not bootstrap. Any joint refit (new data or new model) re-estimates every non-anchor mu, so '去年的模型今天还是同一个 mu' holds only if you never refit - which defeats the design's own batch layer.
R1.evidence: design-grok.md:39 ('Chatbot Arena 因此从在线 Elo 改成了全量 Bradley–Terry MLE'), :194 ('旧模型不会因为新模型进场而被系统性拉下去'), :73 (3-5 frozen anchors). Report progress as delta-mu within one joint fit, or publish refit-versioned / time-windowed boards (Arena's Full vs Latest practice), instead of promising a frozen historical mu. Drop the 'Arena freezes old models' justification entirely.
R1.correction: Verified verbatim against arXiv:2403.04132 (ar5iv HTML): 'Without loss of generality, we take xi_1=0'; 'We made this change because the BT coefficients are better for the purpose of statistical estimation'; the MLE sums over all T battles (Eq. 7); and 'we choose to deploy the sandwich intervals due to their smaller size in large samples' with pivot bootstrap as the comparator. So Arena does not pin 3-5 frozen-mu anchors, does not hold old models' published mu fixed, and the paper does not attribute the switch to online-Elo order-dependence/drift. Design B's line 39 and 194 rationale is therefore factually wrong, and the critic's central point stands: the BT gauge pins the coordinate xi_1, every non-anchor coefficient is re-estimated on every refit. Minor caveats: one cannot prove drift was not a secondary motive, only that the design's causal claim is absent from the source; and the repo's single RandomBot=0 gauge is itself exactly 'one coordinate pinned', so the critic's own real invariant (pin the gauge, not the estimates) is what ADR-0012 already does.

R1.claim: The 'anchors carry the absolute scale' budget is near-useless for ranking in this repo. The only gauge is RandomBot at mu=0, roughly 1300-1450 points below every candidate; the Gaussian PL prediction saturates, so a game against it carries about 5e7x less ranking information than a near-even game at sigma=200, and effectively zero at converged sigma. Design B's 25% anchor allocation and 'scale identifiable' acceptance test therefore buy almost no discrimination between candidates, and the repo already ranks candidates through paired candidate-vs-candidate cross games for exactly this reason.

R1.correction: The premise is a scale error and the magnitude is wrong by ~7 orders. The on-disk manifest is the pre-ADR-0012 1000-based scale (random=1000, lvl4=1429.7); ADR-0012 shifts every absolute rating -1000, so the live gauge is RandomBot=0 with lvl1-lvl4 about 129-448 (ADR-0012 consequence bullet), i.e. a gap of ~430, not 1300-1450. Against the live gauge predict_win(429.7, sigma=200 vs 0)=0.9603, and one game carries Fisher info 3.21e-6 vs 6.37e-6 for an even sigma=200 game: ratio ~2 (gap 500 gives ~3; even at converged sigma~97 it is ~10). The repo also does not rank candidates on the gauge: build_ladder defaults cross=games_per_anchor (ladder.py:567-568), and ADR-0012:51 calls cross=0 the caller's degenerate usage. R1.claim: The proposed CI recipe ('resample battles with replacement, rerun the MLE') is the naive independence bootstrap this repo has already rejected. If the MLE is not yet built, replay from a canonical documented sort order and stop advertising path-independence; the repo's study.py freeze rule ('ratings frozen by default, explicit refit override') is the existing guardrail to reuse.

R1.claim: Design A's SPRT gate turns the pool and anchor set into a selected sample: checkpoints that pass are rated and promoted on the same noisy test that accepted them, inflating accepted strengths by +12 to +45 Elo (same order as the repo's 10-20 Elo action thresholds) and injecting that bias into any accepted checkpoint later used as an anchor.

Since the gate is the only rating data, the published mu is conditional on passing. Reproducible simulation of the design's own SPRT (alpha=beta=0.05, p0=0.5, p1=0.55), `/tmp/review/c_sprt.py`: true p=0.50 -> 4.9% accepted but E[observed Elo | accept]=+45.4; true p=0.525 (+17.4 Elo truth) -> 48.8% accepted, E[Elo|accept]=+38.0, i.e. +20.6 Elo winner's curse; true p=0.55 (+34.9) -> +12.1 Elo bias (mean stopping n=543-913). Repo scale of the problem: evaluation-protocol-validation.md §5 '20 Elo: 50% power 395, 80% power 807' deals; §6 with a +20 point-estimate gate power=0.47 at k=3x400. The selection bias is therefore not a correction: it is as large as the measured effect, and because Gemini promotes accepted checkpoints to anchors, it propagates into the ruler itself.
R1.fix: Split the samples: accept on sample A, then rate/publish the checkpoint on an independent held-out sample B (the repo already has separate qualify and mass phases; the arena's rate_pool/load_round_games provide the independent history). Always log and report rejected checkpoints. Pre-register alpha, H1 and the number of generations tested (alpha spending). Do not derive anchors from test outcomes: choose milestone anchors by generation index (Gemini's own static mechanism) or by time, blind to the SPRT result.
R1.correction: The winner's-curse math is correct and fully reproducible (c_sprt.py: p=0.50 -> 4.9% accept, E[Elo|accept]=+45.4; p=0.525 -> 48.8% accept, +20.6 Elo bias; p=0.55 -> +12.1 Elo bias), and the repo's power numbers quoted (§5 20 Elo 50% power 395 / 80% 807; §6 +20 gate power 0.474 at k=3x400) are accurate. But the fatal claim misreads Design A: its SPRT runs vs the current Best, while the published Elo comes from the separate '与锚点池对弈以确立无漂移 Elo' layer, so the published anchor ratings are NOT computed on the same noisy test that accepted them and are not inflated by it; the design already separates accept and rate samples. Valid residual concerns (narrow the finding to these): (i) if the SPRT's stopping-time observed winrate is reported as the improvement magnitude, it is upward-biased by the simulated +12..+45 Elo; (ii) screening many checkpoints without pre-registered alpha spending inflates family-wise false accepts; (iii) choosing anchor candidates by the gate makes the anchor SET a non-random (stronger) subset, though each anchor's independently measured value stays unbiased. The proposed fix is largely redundant for Design A as written; apply it only if SPRT games feed the rating. Relevance to the PPO repo is partial (the repo selects models by the validated h2h+CI protocol, not SPRT). Confidence medium.

Keep the 25%-anchor quota as a pre-registered schedule constraint, not a score. Report schedule/phase variance alongside sampling variance, and never compare across schedules with a single-fit SE; the repo convention is >=2 seeds/seats or direct h2h.
R1.correction: The substantive claim is sound and repo-relevant: Design A's match_score = -mu_diff + 5.0*is_anchor selects anchors regardless of information, the repo's placement rule is instead Fisher information p(1-p) (opponents.py select_opponent, 'info maximises β²·p(1−p)'), and the reproduced numbers hold (distance 0 -> p(1-p)=0.2500; 200 -> 0.0725 = 29.0%; 300 -> 0.0167 = 6.7%; test_a_far_anchor_carries_little_information moves <5 points). R1.claim: Design B's advertised bootstrap resamples individual battles i.i.d., which understates the interval because twin games on the same deal (and LLM evaluations on the same task) are strongly correlated; in this repo the measured deal-cluster half-width is 1.40x the naive i.i.d. game half-width.

Cross-check bootstrap SE against seed-to-seed/opening-cluster sd and report the max (the repo's `_combine_metric` rule), since that is what achieved >=95% coverage in the 40-seed null; never resample individual battles i.i.d.

My synthetic twin-deal check gives half-width ratio 1.338 (theoretical sqrt(1+rho)=1.342 at rho=0.8), so the exact 1.40x is dataset-dependent but the direction is robust. R1.claim: Both designs mix hard coordinate anchors with soft/measured anchors, so there is no single well-defined scale: hard pins at sigma=0 pretend measured anchor values are error-free and force their inconsistencies into all free ratings, while soft L2 anchors leave the scale set by lambda and by which anchors happen to be in the pool.
R1.evidence: design-grok.md §7: 'μ_anchor = c_anchor（钉死）...多个锚点用软约束：Σ(μ_a − c_a)² 进先验'; design-gemini.md §1 pins static and milestone anchors with sigma=0 and '强行丢弃 Anchor 的更新结果'. Repo ADR-0012: '锚点值不是“标定出来的”，而是表的坐标基准...只保留一个钉死的坐标基准，其余一切由对局估计'; src/seven523/ladder.py plan_games: 'a ladder needs at least one pinned anchor for identifiability', and its docstring notes candidate ranking comes from `cross` games once there is a single gauge. Under hard pins the anchor MLE has no slack: if two pinned values are mutually inconsistent with the observed outcomes, only the free ratings can absorb the error, all of it; under soft pins the location optimum of sum log L + lambda*sum(mu_a - c_a)^2 moves with lambda and with anchor-set composition, i.e. the ruler moves when the pool changes. Neither design propagates anchor uncertainty into the reported delta-mu CIs (sigma=0 means zero by fiat).
R1.fix: Keep exactly one hard gauge whose value is a definition (RandomBot=0, ADR-0012); treat all other frozen snapshots as free parameters or soft-prior nodes and report delta-mu with the joint information matrix (the repo already fixed free-free double counting in elo.py's information assembly, evaluation-protocol-validation.md §4). If the machine needs 'absolute' error bars, propagate anchor posterior uncertainty by parametric bootstrap of the anchor values. Version-key the ruler (task/rules version) so a changed instrument starts a new scale, as study.py and ADR-0011 already require.
R1.correction: The core is right and repo-relevant: Design A pins multiple anchors with sigma=0 and discards their updates; if two pins are mutually inconsistent with observed outcomes only free ratings absorb all the error; and neither design propagates anchor uncertainty into reported delta-mu intervals. ADR-0012 mandates exactly one hard gauge ('只保留一个钉死的坐标基准，其余一切由对局估计'), and ladder.plan_games requires >=1 pinned anchor for identifiability. Two overstatements to narrow: (i) Design B does not merely mix hard and soft anchors in a way that leaves the scale lambda-dependent — §7 hard-pins one anchor when there is a single DOF ('只有一个自由度时，等价于某个锚点=25') and uses soft L2 constraints only for additional snapshots, which is the ADR-0012 single-gauge rule; the gauge is fixed by the hard pin, lambda affects only the extra anchors' compromise, so the finding is fully strict only for Design A. (ii) The suggested repo fix ('joint information matrix... elo.py's information assembly, evaluation-protocol-validation.md §4') refers to the BT-MAP Hessian that ADR-0011 explicitly deleted; the current estimator has no information matrix and reports OpenSkill sigma, not CIs, so that fix needs re-grounding (parametric bootstrap of anchor values, as the critic also proposes, is the workable route). Confidence high.

R1.claim: Gemini's conservative rating mu - 3*sigma is a games-played statistic, not a strength statistic, when sigmas are unequal: at fixed mu it rises ~395 project points from 0 to 40 games purely because sigma shrinks, so any ranking or gate on it reintroduces time drift and selects for measurement history rather than ability.
R1.evidence: design-gemini.md §2: `conservative_rating = mu - 3*sigma` with docstring '保守等级分，常用于排位与门禁判定 (mu - 3*sigma)'. Reproducible `/tmp/review/a_openskill.py` on the repo config (mu=500, sigma=200, beta=100, tau=2): sigma is 200 at n=0, 154.8 at n=4, 68.4 at n=40 against a pinned anchor, so mu-3*sigma moves +600 -> +336 over 40 games with the candidate's true strength and mu unchanged; a sigma=0 pinned anchor is charged nothing (full mu). Any gate comparing a fresh candidate to a converged one starts the fresh model 600 points behind. Design B already rejects this for progress ('比较进步用 μ 和胜率，不用 ordinal'), but Gemini uses it for ladder placement and gating.
R1.fix: Compare models with mu and intervals from the joint information matrix (or direct paired h2h), not with mu-3*sigma. If a conservative display is wanted, restrict comparisons to models with comparable sigma/history and state the decision rule; never use the ordinal as an accept/reject or promotion gate, and never as an 'improvement' measure.
R1.correction: The property is correct: mu-3sigma is a history/uncertainty statistic, and on the repo scale sigma is 200 at n=0, 154.8 at n=4, 68.4 at n=40 vs a pinned anchor, so the lower bound moves ~388 points at fixed-ish mu (mu 493.6): 500-3*200 = -100 at n=0 -> 288.3 at n=40; the 3-sigma penalty drops 600 -> 205, i.e. ~395 points. However the critic's stated endpoints are not reproducible: '+600 -> +336' does not match any probe (the correct figures are -100 -> +288 for mu-3sigma, or a 600 -> 205 penalty), and 'starts the fresh model 600 points behind' conflates the fresh model's own 3-sigma penalty (600) with its gap to a converged peer (~388 at n=40, up to ~500 at the repo tau floor), not 600. Also Design A only DEFINES conservative_rating and states its intended use in a docstring ('常用于排位与门禁判定'); the pasted code never calls it, and Design A's actual gate is SPRT winrate, so 'Gemini uses it for ladder placement and gating' rests on stated intent rather than demonstrated code. The recommendation (compare mu/intervals or direct h2h, never gate on the ordinal) is sound. Confidence high.

R1.claim: Neither design's acceptance suite can falsify 'no drift': Design B's tests are code invariants plus unfalsifiable prose ('almost unchanged', 'within 2 sigma') with no power, coverage or equivalence margin, Design A has no test, and neither controls multiplicity across the many checkpoints being screened.
R1.evidence: design-grok.md §8 rows: '锚点不动 ... 锚点 μ 变化 = 0（在线层写回）', '顺序无关 ... 公布 μ 差 < 1e-6', 'τ 关闭 ... μ 漂移 ≈ 0', and the unfalsifiable '旧模型不背锅 ... 第一个新模型的公布 μ 几乎不动（MLE 层）' plus single-run '校准后 μ̂ 落在 Δ 的 2σ 内'; design-gemini.md has no acceptance test at all. The repo's measurement plan shows what is required and what the numbers are: evaluation-protocol-validation.md §3.2 builds an independent-random null over 40 seeds (single-run 95% CI coverage 37/40=92.5%; pooled k=2/3/5 coverage 20/20, 13/13, 8/8); §5 gives the power table ('20 Elo: 50% power 395, 80% power 807 deals', '10 Elo: 80% 3226'); §6 measures Delta=20 power=0.47 with the +20 gate and 0.78 CI-only at k=3x400; §8 warns '多对筛选 ... 筛 20 对期望 ~0.35 个假阳'. Candidate screening compounds it: with the repo's h2h sigma_400=10.14 Elo and independent estimates, E[max] of k equal candidates is +11.8 Elo (k=5), +15.6 (k=10), +18.9 (k=20) in pure noise (/tmp/review/f_maxk.py; shared deals would reduce but not remove the effect). 'mu almost unchanged' and '2 sigma' have no stated n, so they cannot be failed by data.
R1.fix: Replace the invariant table with a null-injection test through the whole pipeline: run identical weights under two ids through matchmaking, gating and publication, across >=3 independent seeds x >=400 deals; pre-register an equivalence margin (e.g. |delta-mu| < 10 Elo) and require (a) 95% CI coverage of 0 >=95% and (b) no outcome-conditional shift in acceptance/publication. Size it from the repo's sigma_N=sigma_400*sqrt(400/N) (Delta=20 Elo needs ~807 deals/arm for 80% power). Pre-register the number of candidate comparisons and use Holm/Bonferroni or independent-seed replication for any claimed winner; treat any single-seed 'significant' result as a screen, not a conclusion.
R1.correction: Confirmed with minor clarifications. Verified in the designs: Design A has no acceptance/validation test at all; Design B's §8 table is mostly invariants ('锚点 μ 变化 = 0', 'μ 差 < 1e-6', 'σ 不回升') plus unfalsifiable prose ('几乎不动', '2σ 内') with no n/power/coverage/equivalence margin. All cited repo numbers check out (evaluation-protocol-validation.md §3.2 single-run 37/40=92.5%, pooled k=2/3/5 = 20/20,13/13,8/8; §5 20 Elo 50% power 395 / 80% 807, 10 Elo 80% 3226; §6 +20 gate power 0.474 vs CI-only 0.776; §8 '筛 20 对期望 ~0.35 个假阳'), and f_maxk.py reproduces (+11.8/+15.6/+18.9 Elo for k=5/10/20 at sigma_400=10.14). Clarifications: Design B has no accept/reject gate, so 'neither controls multiplicity across the many checkpoints being screened' applies specifically to Design A's SPRT (no alpha spending) and to k-candidate winner selection in both; the E[max] figures assume independent per-candidate errors whereas plan_games shares deal seeds across candidates (positive correlation reduces but does not remove the effect, as the critic notes); sizing from sigma_N=sigma_400*sqrt(400/N) is correct. Confidence high.

R2.claim: The round-1 flagship remedy — code:AB-no-batch-MLE's 'implement a genuine batch estimator beside fit_ratings ... e.g. scipy L-BFGS on the Plackett-Luce likelihood', echoed by stats:F2, practice-chess:F1, requirements:A-batch-refit-is-a-loop and repo:grok-mle-second-truth — is exactly the move ADR-0011 rejected, and would break elo.py's documented purity contract. Round-1 proposed it without flagging the ADR conflict or requiring an amendment, so its 'fix' would regress an architectural decision that the repo deliberately made.
R2.evidence: ADR-0011 lines 48-49: 'OpenSkill 没有分差似然；另设第二套似然或逐 id 裁剪会制造第二真相，并与「标准高斯模型」冲突'. ADR-0011 lines 37/68: 'priors 是 D3 唯一注入点、不新增接缝'. src/seven523/elo.py imports only openskill + stdlib (no numpy/scipy anywhere in elo/duel/study/ladder; `grep` returns none), while code:AB-no-batch-MLE's fix literally says 'scipy L-BFGS'. ADR-0011's own rejected-alternatives list names the 'second likelihood'.
R2.fix: Drop the batch-MLE remedy as the default. The repo's scale-free comparison is already duel.paired_duel_stats / combine_duel_seeds (validation §9). If a single global order-free board is a hard product requirement, make it a new ADR that explicitly supersedes ADR-0011's single-likelihood decision, implement it as a standalone pure-Python tool (no numpy/scipy) reading the existing per-game JSONL, and keep it out of elo.py; round-1 must state the ADR conflict and demand the amendment, not prescribe scipy.
R2.correction: Directionally right, but overstated on two counts. (a) A full-history joint/batch estimator does conflict with ADR-0011's single-estimator architecture — decision 1 is literally '在线重放代替联合 MAP' (online replay replaces joint MAP) and the ADR keeps `priors` as the only injection point / no new seams (lines 37, 68). (b) However the cited lines 48-49 reject a *second likelihood* (margin/window) and per-id clipping ('另设第二套似然或逐 id 裁剪…制造第二真相'); a batch Plackett-Luce MLE reuses the same Gaussian PL likelihood, so it is not literally the thing those lines reject — it is a second *estimator/seam*, not a second likelihood. (c) 'Would break elo.py's documented purity contract' holds only if scipy L-BFGS is added inside elo.py; the same finding's own remedy (standalone tool) would not. Verified: no numpy/scipy anywhere in elo/duel/study/ladder; ADR-0011 decision 1 and '不新增接缝' are real. The substantive point stands and is relevant (design-grok §3/§7 proposes exactly a second full-history PL-MLE board), but round-1 should have framed it as a single-estimator/ADR conflict requiring an amendment, not as the already-rejected 'second likelihood'.

R2.claim: Round-1 overstates and misattributes the repo's clustering penalty. stats:F5, redteam:A5 and requirements:both-wrong-clustering-unit present a 1.40x-2.0x CI understatement as 'the' repo design effect and therefore frame both designs as equally wrong. In the repo's current seat-balanced schedule the single-arm bootstrap is already calibrated (~1.0-1.1); the ~2.0 figure is a cross-order/phase effect, and the 1.40x is a synthetic twin-correlation check, not the operating regime. The genuine defect is only Design B's game-level resampling; the repo's deal-clustered bootstrap is the thing the designs should copy.
R2.evidence: docs/experiments/elo-reliability-audit.md §3.5 table: '单臂 bootstrap sd ≈ Fisher SE（20.7 vs 21.7）' and '换序差 sd ≈ √2 × SE'. docs/experiments/evaluation-protocol-validation.md §0 row 2: 'twin 相关时 deal-cluster 半宽是 naive-game 的 1.40×' (a from-scratch check), and §3.2 zero-null: single 400-deal CI covers 0 in 37/40 = 92.5%, merged k=2/3/5 = 100%, ratio seed-sd/bootstrap-sd = 1.11. src/seven523/duel.py:117-118: 'The clustering unit is that twin pair: the bootstrap resamples **deals**'.
R2.fix: Re-scope the finding: cite ~1.0-1.1 for the repo's fixed seat-balanced arm, reserve 1.4x for genuine within-twin residual correlation and 2.0 only for cross-order/cross-fit comparisons. Credit duel.paired_duel_stats as already-correct, and keep the criticism aimed only at Design B's i.i.d. battle resampling.
R2.correction: The repo numbers support the critic's decomposition. Verified: elo-reliability-audit.md §3.5 table gives single-arm clustered bootstrap sd 20.66 vs Fisher SE 21.65 (~0.95x, i.e. calibrated), and evaluation-protocol-validation.md §3.2 gives seed-sd/bootstrap-sd = 1.11; so ~1.0-1.1 for the already-deal-clustered arm is correct. The '2.0' is a *variance* design effect for the cross-order/phase contrast (mean 2.04; 30.66/21.65 = 1.42x in sd), so calling it a '2.0x CI understatement' conflates sd with variance. The 1.40x is validation §0 row 2's deal-cluster-vs-naive-game ratio under twin correlation — and that is exactly the error design-grok incurs when it resamples 战报 i.i.d. (§7.3 '对战报有放回重采样'), so it is not merely synthetic/irrelevant; it is the correction for Design B. duel.py:117-118 does say the bootstrap resamples deals. Caveat: the specific claim about what stats:F5/redteam:A5 presented is not verifiable from the two design files given; only the technical decomposition is verifiable.

R2.claim: The round-1 'fatal' tally is inflated by duplication across lenses and by grading pasted chess/LLM pseudocode as if it were a repo patch. Six findings are the same tau=0 + sigma=0 ZeroDivisionError (stats:F1, repo:grok-tau0-incompatible, practice-llm:B3, code:B-crash-tau0-sigma0, requirements:B-tau-zero-impossible-here, code:B-tau0-no-equilibrium-calibration); about eight are the same batch_recalibrate infinite-loop / not-an-MLE defect (math:gemini-batch-infinite-loop, math:gemini-replay-is-not-mle, stats:F2, repo:gemini-batch-refit-noop, practice-chess:F1, code:A-batch-infinite-loop, code:AB-no-batch-MLE, requirements:A-batch-refit-is-a-loop). Round-1's own corrections repeatedly walk the severity back, so the aggregate 'many fatals' signal is misleading.
R2.evidence: All six tau ids reduce to the same two repros: `FitConfig(tau=0.0)` -> ValueError 'tau must be positive and finite' (elo.py:144-146) and `PlackettLuce(tau=0.0).rate([[sigma=200],[sigma=0]])` -> ZeroDivisionError (I reproduced both). All eight batch ids reduce to `for ... in self.match_history: self.update_match(...)` with `update_match` appending to the same list. Round-1 corrections concede e.g. 'within Grok's own scheme tau=0 is self-consistent' and 'the crash requires an all-sigma=0 team'.
R2.fix: De-duplicate by mechanism and publish one severity per distinct defect. Separate 'bug in illustrative pseudocode of a chess-flavoured design' from 'repo-integration blocker'. For this repo the tau=0 issue is a single major ADR/contract conflict (FitConfig tau>0), not six fatals; likewise the replay bug is one fatal in Design A, not eight findings.
R2.correction: De-duplicating by mechanism is valid and the two root causes are real: FitConfig rejects tau=0 with `ValueError: tau must be positive and finite` (elo.py:144-146), and (in openskill 6.2.0) PlackettLuce(tau=0).rate(...) raises ZeroDivisionError as soon as ANY participant has sigma=0 — I reproduced it with winner sigma=0, loser sigma=0, and both sigma=0; two positive sigmas with tau=0 do NOT crash. So the round-1 concession 'the crash requires an all-sigma=0 team' is too narrow: it requires at least one zero-sigma team. Also the batch group lumps two distinct defects: an actual infinite loop (design-gemini batch_recalibrate iterates self.match_history while update_match appends to it — I reproduced the mutation-during-iteration) and a conceptual flaw (replay is not a genuine MLE). So the honest de-dup is ~2 tau failure modes (repo guard vs openskill crash) and ~2 batch defects, not cleanly 'six→1, eight→1'. The meta-point still holds: the aggregate 'many fatals' tally double-counts lenses and should be published per distinct mechanism.

R2.claim: Two round-1 fixes would edit the frozen pure core to own state it must not own: code:repo-free-ids-drift-inflation's 'Extend fit_ratings/FitConfig with a per-id status map (anchor / established-frozen / probation)' and redteam:A8's 'Hash the rules/task content into every PlayedGame row, every manifest, and every fit record'. ADR-0011 keeps `priors` as the only injection point and forbids new seams; ADR-0006 fixes PlayedGame as (seed, seats, scores). The repo already reaches both goals at the correct layer, and round-1 did not flag the ADR conflict.
R2.evidence: ADR-0011 lines 37/68: 'priors 是 D3 唯一注入点、不新增接缝'; ADR-0006 line 29: '不新增接缝'. src/seven523/elo.py: PlayedGame fields are exactly `seed, seats, scores`. src/seven523/study.py merge_manifest freezes levels by default ('frozen per id unless refit is set'). src/seven523/trace.py:177 already embeds `"rules": rules_json(rules)`; only the ladder results JSONL lacks it, i.e. the fix belongs at the orchestration layer.
R2.fix: Leave elo.py's dataclasses and signatures alone. Add a rules/task version tag on the ladder/study manifest and refuse cross-version pooling there; express warm-start/freeze purely through the existing Prior/anchors + manifest refit path. Round-1 should label these two fixes as layer mistakes that contradict ADR-0011/ADR-0006.
R2.correction: Confirmed on substance. Verified: ADR-0011 lines 37/68 keep `priors` as the only injection point and forbid new seams; elo.py PlayedGame fields are exactly (seed, seats, scores); study.merge_manifest freezes levels/subject mu by default (`setdefault` unless refit=True); trace.build_trace already sets "rules": rules_json(rules) (trace.py:177); the ladder per-game results JSONL (ladder.py:339-350) has no rules field. Minor citation error: the (seed, seats, scores) shape is defined by ADR-0011/elo.py, not ADR-0006 (whose line 29 is the no-new-seam commitment and which is in any case superseded by ADR-0011/0012). Adding a per-id status map to fit_ratings/FitConfig, or a rules hash into every PlayedGame row, would indeed add a new seam/observation field to the frozen pure core; both goals are expressible at the orchestration layer (anchors/Prior + manifest refit; rules tag on the ladder/study manifest). The finding is relevant and correctly scoped.

R2.claim: requirements:both-miss-the-measured-drift is rated fatal, but it is a gap in the two designs' drift taxonomy and acceptance tests, not a live repo defect: the repo already fixed the deterministic candidate-index seat-phase drift (0-75 Elo) with seat-rotated twin deals and already clusters uncertainty by deal. Round-1's own correction concedes 'the repo has already remediated this exact defect ... so fatal is arguable'. Rating it fatal overstates the repository-level harm.
R2.evidence: src/seven523/ladder.py plan_games schedules each deal seed twice via `for seat in (0, 1)` with the candidate on each seat; tests/test_ladder.py::test_plan_games_is_order_invariant_and_seat_balanced asserts twins and permutation invariance; evaluation-protocol-validation.md §0 row 1: '3 种候选顺序的拟合值逐位相同；每个 (候选,锚点,牌) twin 座位恰好 [0,1]'.
R2.fix: Downgrade to major and reframe as 'the designs lack a drift taxonomy and regression gate'; the deliverable is the taxonomy (location / order / intransitivity / true improvement / rules change) plus promoting the existing permutation regression to a release gate — not a new remediation.
R2.correction: The reframing is correct, with one caveat. Verified: ladder.plan_games schedules each deal seed twice for `seat in (0,1)` (ladder.py:159-165); tests/test_ladder.py::test_plan_games_is_order_invariant_and_seat_balanced asserts permutation invariance and [0,1] twin seats; evaluation-protocol-validation.md §0 row 1 confirms identical fitted values across 3 candidate orders. So the deterministic candidate-index seat-phase drift (audit 0-75 Elo) is already remediated and uncertainty is already deal-clustered, hence 'fatal' as a *live repo defect* overstates harm. Caveat: the audit's remediation was on the retired BT-MAP estimator, but the seat-phase mechanism is estimator-agnostic and the current code implements it; and it remains a genuine gap in the two designs' drift taxonomy/acceptance tests (neither adds a regression gate). Downgrading to major and reframing as 'designs lack a drift taxonomy and gate' is the right call.

R2.claim: repo:fix-improvement-gate recommends adding a new pure `duel.sprt_decision(...)` accept gate, and requirements:A-answers-wrong-decision-for-ranking assumes the repo needs an automated gate. It does not: there is no automated promotion gate and the repo's own validated protocol already decides 'worth acting on' with a fixed-sample deal-clustered head-to-head CI. Importing Design A's SPRT adds multiplicity risk and machinery without addressing the drift question, and round-1 elsewhere shows it uses the retired 400-logistic scale.
R2.evidence: `grep -rn -i sprt src tools tests docs` returns nothing outside PPO rollout batching. evaluation-protocol-validation.md §9 fixes the rule: '≥3 seed × 400 副牌 ... 95% CI ... CI 完全排除 0 且点估计 ≥ +10'; duel.paired_duel_stats already returns the deal-clustered winrate CI plus an exact per-deal sign-test p-value.
R2.fix: Do not build an SPRT. If automated promotion is genuinely wanted, wire the existing duel CI / combine_duel_seeds into the caller and pre-register the rule; label SPRT as Design A's chess heritage and out of scope for this repo.
R2.correction: Confirmed. `grep -rn -i sprt src tools tests docs` returns nothing. There is no automated promotion/accept gate in league.py/ladder.py (grep for promot/gate/accept finds nothing; PfspController is opponent sampling, not promotion). evaluation-protocol-validation.md §9 fixes the rule as >=3 seed x 400 deals, merged 95% CI, CI excludes 0 AND point estimate >= +10 (>=20 needs 5x400 / 3x800). duel.paired_duel_stats already returns the deal-clustered winrate/elo CI and combine_duel_seeds the multi-seed merge (max(bootstrap SE, between-seed sd)/sqrt(k)*z); _binomial_two_sided_p gives the per-deal sign test. Design A's SPRT H1 p>=0.55 maps to ~35 Elo on the retired 400-logistic scale (400*log10(.55/.45)=34.9). One nuance: SPRT itself is not inherently multiplicity-prone — it controls error rates if pre-registered with a spending rule; the objection is scope/new machinery and using a retired scale, not a mathematical defect. The recommendation (use the existing CI/sign-test protocol rather than build SPRT) is sound for this repo.

R2.claim: math:logistic-vs-probit-link is a real observation, but its remedy — 'For WL updates, calibrate/report the logistic probability implied by rate ... do not use predict_win as the target' — if applied to this repo, inverts ADR-0011 decision 2, which deliberately made expected_score = predict_win the single probability model to avoid a split between the update link and the pairing/reporting link. The finding matters only inside designs that validate a logistic update with predict_win, not as a repo change.
R2.evidence: Reproduced: A=(600,200), B=(500,200), beta=100 -> c=316.227766, predict_win=0.624085, logistic(100/c)=0.578405, gap 4.568 pp. ADR-0011 line 48 rejects '更新用高斯、选档用 logistic' and says '改用 predict_win 保证单一真相'.
R2.fix: For the repo keep predict_win as the single truth and, at most, document that it is the probit model's probability rather than the softmax update. Scope the round-1 fix to design reporting only and explicitly note it must not invert ADR-0011.
R2.correction: Confirmed exactly. Reproduced with A=(600,200), B=(500,200), beta=100: c=316.227766, predict_win=0.624085, logistic(100/c)=0.578405, gap=4.568pp. openskill 6.2.0 source confirms the split: PlackettLuce.predict_win uses phi_major (probit) while the update's _sum_q uses math.exp(adjusted_mu/c) (softmax/logistic). ADR-0011 lines 48-52 explicitly reject '更新用高斯、选档用 logistic' and keep expected_score=predict_win as the single truth, so applying the round-1 remedy to the repo WOULD invert that decision. Caveat: the finding is largely a no-op for the repo as-is — design-grok already reports `predict_win` (§7.2) and the repo's expected_score is predict_win, so the remedy only matters as a per-design reporting caveat. Correct scope: keep predict_win as the repo's single probability model; do not retarget it.

R2.claim: Steelmanned, both designs' central insight — separate the online/matchmaking layer from the published scale, pin one gauge, and compare order-free — is almost entirely what the repo already did: ADR-0011 (OpenSkill core with order dependence documented), ADR-0012 (single RandomBot gauge), seat-rotated twin deals, deal-clustered head-to-head, manifest freeze with explicit refit. The minimal viable change set is documentation plus a version tag, not a second estimator. 'Do nothing' is defensible because pairwise comparison is already scale-free and order-free, and published values are already frozen.
R2.evidence: src/seven523/duel.py docstring / paired_duel_stats (scale-free deal-clustered h2h); src/seven523/study.py merge_manifest default freeze; src/seven523/ladder.py plan_games seat twins; docs/adr/0012-single-gauge-and-greedy-removal.md; evaluation-protocol-validation.md §9 recommended ≥3 seed × 400-deal h2h protocol.
R2.fix: MVP (low cost): (1) a short drift-taxonomy ADR stating what 'no drift' means and that h2h is the comparison channel; (2) a rules/task version tag on the ladder/study manifest with refusal to pool across versions; (3) if a decision gate is wanted, wire the existing combine_duel_seeds. Do nothing (zero cost): keep h2h + manifest freeze + single gauge and publish no absolute cross-fit banner. Only build a batch MLE if a single global order-free board is a hard product requirement — and then via a new ADR, pure-Python, separate tool (high cost: new ADR + optimizer + validation + permanent second-estimator maintenance).
R2.correction: The overlap is real and large, but the 'almost entirely already done / documentation+tag is the MVP / do nothing' framing is overstated. Verified already present: online OpenSkill (elo.fit_ratings), single pinned RandomBot gauge (ADR-0012), seat-rotated twin deals (ladder.plan_games), deal-clustered order-free head-to-head (duel.paired_duel_stats; docstring: input order irrelevant), manifest freeze (study.merge_manifest), and the >=3x400 CI protocol (validation §9). But the repo does NOT have: any rules/task version tag on the ladder results JSONL or manifest (only trace documents carry rules), a documented drift taxonomy, or a global batch board; and design-grok's model-lifecycle states/family priors are genuine additions.
